summary: Adds tenant-aware SSO engine assignments, fine-grained authorization, governed engine modes, mandatory identity reconciliation, and portable headless provisioning.
userImpact: Administrators can map identity-provider groups to engines, Engine Sets, runtime resources, and runtime-resource sets.
Mission Control enforces resource-type permissions and independently controls whether process variables are hidden, visible, or editable.
Managed memberships clearly indicate whether access is controlled manually, by SSO, or by configuration, and configuration-owned controls become view-only.
The login experience uses provider display names, supports safe single-provider redirection, hides disabled local login, and keeps administrator recovery separate.

instructions: Back up the application database and configuration before upgrading.
Allow the application to run the TypeORM authorization, identity, and engine-governance migrations; do not execute hand-written database-specific SQL.
Review existing engine registrations and assign explicit tenancy before using the external engine provisioning API.
Review SSO mappings, engine authority modes, configuration ownership, and break-glass administrator membership before enabling SSO enforcement.
Retain the generated migration, authorization, identity-reconciliation, and image-security evidence with the release record.

configuration: Adds JSON configuration for identity providers, identity mappings, provider display and login labels, login behavior, engine registration, engine tenancy, governance ownership, and reconciliation.
Adds enterprise-authoritative, engine-native, mirrored-backstop, and credentialless customer-sidecar engine integration settings.
Configuration-managed providers, mappings, roles, grants, engines, and governance settings are presented as configuration-owned and cannot be mutated through the portal.

changes: Adds OpenAPI-described headless endpoints and schemas for SSO providers, mappings, engines, authority modes, tenancy, resource assignments, effective access, and reconciliation.
Tenant-scoped login discovery and provider-start routes are additive; the global default-tenant routes remain compatibility aliases.
External engine registration and idempotent upsert now require explicit tenancy instead of inferring the default tenant.
The enterprise plugin API adds a portable TypeORM database context while retaining the legacy connectionPool field as deprecated compatibility.

migrations: Authorization, identity, and engine-governance migration series through 1700000000107
notes: Clean install, upgrade, interrupted retry, schema equivalence, service behavior, rollback, and cleanup are qualified across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and Spanner.
Existing SSO rows and the OSS default-tenant fallback are preserved; compatibility aliases remain where documented.

security: Identity-provider entitlements are reconciled after every successful OIDC, Entra-compatible OIDC, SAML, and LDAP login so removed grants are revoked promptly.
Tenant and resource boundaries are enforced in the backend, including sibling and cross-tenant denials.
Process-variable redaction is performed by the backend before values reach EnterpriseGlue clients.
Engine endpoints, sidecar trust boundaries, configuration secrets, callback state, sessions, and break-glass access have fail-closed validation and dedicated regression coverage.
documentation: Headless API and JSON configuration: `docs/reference/access-governance-and-headless-api.md` and `docs/architecture/11-json-driven-authz-and-engine-registration.md`
Release contribution and fail-fast CI preflight: `docs/development/release-notes-process.md`
knownLimitations: Protected real-OpenShift evidence remains deferred by release decision.
Real customer identity-provider credentials are not stored in CI; provider-specific behavior is covered with disposable local protocol services and Entra-compatible emulation.
rollback: Roll back backend and frontend images together and run the documented TypeORM migration rollback for the matching application version.
Preserve classification reports, transition previews, mapping versions, reconciliation summaries, and release evidence before rollback.
Do not repair engine topology, ownership, or SSO state with direct database edits.
validation: Backend and frontend unit, integration, typecheck, lint, and browser suites
PostgreSQL and Oracle CI plus five-adapter migration and runtime portability qualification
OIDC, Entra-compatible OIDC, SAML, and LDAP login, mapping, reconciliation, grant, revocation, and denial scenarios
Fine-grained authorization state-space, custom-role, resource-type, machine-principal, variable-control, and mutation coverage
Operaton and Camunda mirrored-backstop matrix plus local real-Operaton and customer-sidecar container evidence
Reusable release-note preflight contracts and dependency ordering across every expensive pull-request workflow
Versioned Codex plugin, skill metadata, portability, PR-readiness, UI-evidence, access-governance lane selection, and contract-parity helper contracts
Built-image deployment smoke, CodeQL, third-party notices, package compatibility, and hardened image security scans
